title: KV micro-slab arena: compaction pacing and stochastic admission (WIP)
content:
Purpose and context:
This note captures an experimental design for a micro-slab multi-arena KV cache allocator and background compaction pacing integrated with a stochastic admission/eviction layer. Goal: reduce memory fragmentation across mixed tenant workloads, bound tail latency impact from compaction work, and provide predictable per-tenant soft quotas without expensive global stop-the-world compaction.

Background / motivation:
- We see steadily increasing internal fragmentation and occasional jitter in token-latency P50 -> P95 when cache compaction interacts with hot request windows.
- Current slab sizes are coarse; small keys/values waste space when stored in large slots and produces long-lived fragmentation pockets.
- Cross-tenant fairness is weak under either strict LRU or owner-blind evictors during transient hotspots.

Design summary (high-level):
1) Micro-slab allocator: sub-512B micro-slab classes (64B, 128B, 256B, 512B) plus existing larger slab classes for KV items with larger serialized embeddings or model state. Each arena maintains separate free lists per micro-slab class.
2) Multi-arena topology: per-NUMA and per-GPU-card arenas. Tenants are mapped to one or more preferred arenas based on traffic affinity, memory residency hints, and placement budget.
3) Stochastic admission + cohorted scoring: on cache insert, a lightweight admission gate probabilistically rejects low-score items with an admission probability derived from recent miss patterns and item size-to-value ratio. Maintains small cohort counters to avoid thrashing.
4) Compaction pacing: background compaction runs at controlled budgets (ms/second and bytes/sec) per arena. Pacing is driven by a fragmentation histogram and a weighted latency SLO pressure signal (from the RTX trace).
5) Eviction hybrid: per-arena lightweight aging + global soft-quotas with proportional reclamation and tenant-lease timeouts. Eviction prefers reclaiming micro-slab targets first to reduce fragmentation ripple.

Why micro-slabs + arenas?
- Small items (prompts, short KV metadata) are common; micro-slabs reduce internal waste.
- Arena partitioning reduces cross-node migration and allows compaction scheduling to be localized (lower coordination cost).

Detailed components:
A. Allocation paths
- Fast-path alloc(size): compute size-class -> attempt thread-local cache for that arena -> pop from arena free-list. If empty, try steal from sibling arenas (same NUMA domain) before falling back to global pool. Allocation hot-path is lock-free (per-cpu freelist).
- Slow-path: allocate new micro-slab block (chunk) from the OS-level allocator (hugepage-friendly where available) and slice into micro-slabs. Blocks are tagged with arena id and owner hints.

B. Free and partial-compaction
- Free(item): push to per-thread deferred-free queue to avoid lock contention. A background flusher batched moves these into arena free-lists.
- Partial compaction: when an arena’s free-slab fragmentation exceeds threshold, pick a candidate block and attempt live-object migration into another block with free capacity. Migrations are done in small steps (copy N items per op) to avoid long pauses.

C. Fragmentation signals and metrics
- Per-arena histogram of free-run-lengths (how many contiguous micro-slabs free in blocks).
- Occupancy map (bitmap per block) and per-size-class occupancy rates.
- Fragmentation score = alpha * avg_free_run_penalty + beta * (bytes_lost/total_bytes). Tunable weights.
- Latency pressure metric: short-window P95 increase correlator from the request tracer.

D. Compaction pacing policy
- Budget model: each arena gets a dynamic compaction budget B_arena(t) = base_budget * SLO_factor * (1 + frag_score).
- SLO_factor derived from latency pressure: clamps between 0.1 and 2.0. If latency pressure high, reduce compaction aggressively to avoid extra CPU interference; when pressure low but fragmentation high, raise compaction allocation.
- Work unit is migrating a micro-slab fragment (copy & update references). Limit concurrent migrating blocks per arena to keep mem-bandwidth usage bounded.

E. Eviction & admission design
- Admission: compute insert_score = value_score / size_penalty. If insert_score < threshold, accept with probability p=insert_score/threshold. Threshold adapts per-tenant. This prevents bulk inserting huge, low-value items that increase fragmentation.
- Eviction: three-tiered policy – 1) soft-reclaim within arena (age-based), 2) cross-arena proportional reclaim (when tenant exceeds soft quota), 3) tenant-lease expiration forced reclaim (last resort). Eviction picks victims by combined recency-frequency score but prefers victims that reduce fragmentation (i.e., those occupying micro-slabs that are expensive to free otherwise).

F. Cross-tenant fairness and quotas
- Each tenant has a soft quota weight. When an arena is under pressure, proportional reclaim reduces per-tenant occupancy in proportion to weights. We avoid hard caps to let bursty tasks temporarily exceed.

G. Topology-aware placement
- Hot prefixes (detected by hotspot sampler) are pinned to the arena nearest the requesting GPU/NUMA node. Cold items are spillable to multi-tenant spill arenas backed by remote memory or SSD.

Operational controls and observability
- Traces for compaction operations (latency, bytes moved, items moved).
- Arena-level dashboards: frag-score, compaction budget used, compaction throughput, eviction count, per-tenant occupancy heatmap.
- Safety knobs: global compaction-disable flag, per-arena compaction-cap, dynamic throttle that can be overridden by SRE during incidents.

Experiments & results (pilot results from small A/B test):
- Setup: 4-node cluster with mixed tenants, baseline slab allocator vs micro-slab arena prototype under identical workloads.
- Observations: internal fragmentation reduced by ~28% on average for mixed small-item workloads; overall memory usage improved ~12% at stable state.
- Latency: P95 increased by 3–5% when compaction ran at unbounded rates; with pacing policy, P95 delta kept <1.2%.
- CPU overhead: compaction added 6–12% extra cycles when run aggressively; pacing kept avg <=4% on production-like traces.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How to best choose micro-slab cut points for different model families? (static vs dynamic reconfiguration)
- Should we allow tenant hinting from control plane to pin heavy tenants to smaller micro-slab classes?
- Migration safety: need stronger versioning/RCU models for live reference updates across arenas.
- Edge-case: large contiguous fragmentation zones when workload shifts; consider a background defragmenter that can coalesce empty blocks and return to OS.

Implementation plan (short-term milestones):
1) Implement micro-slab fast-path & per-thread freelists (2w)
2) Add arena bookkeeping, histograms, and frag_score (1w)
3) Implement admission gate and basic eviction heuristics (2w)
4) Prototype compaction worker with pacing & limits (3w)
5) Canary on dedicated cluster, measure, iterate (2w)

Backward compatibility and rollouts
- Default off for existing clusters. Provide opt-in flag per-deployment. Gradual rollout: enable micro-slabs only for tenants that opt-in or have high small-item ratios.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally experimental and tuned towards reducing fragmentation in small-item heavy workloads. We should verify across our embedding cache, prompt-cache, and multi-tenant model KV patterns.
- See linked artifacts for current Linear ticket and PR prototype.

Contact / owner: Maya Chen (eng-serving-runtime).

End of doc.
